study.title: The efficacy and cerebral mechanism of intradermal acupuncture for major depressive disorder: a multicenter randomized controlled trial
study.article_type: randomized controlled trial with nested neuroimaging substudy
study.study_design: multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial (RCT) with nested fMRI substudy (non-repeated event-related [NRER] paradigm)
study.randomization: Randomly allocated by SPSS 25 software in a 1:1:1 ratio. Randomization was stratified by gender and age with a block size of 6. An independent assistant placed random numbers in sealed envelopes.
study.blinding: Participants, outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to group allocation; acupuncturists were not blinded. For the MRI study, randomization and blinding were not applicable.
study.population: participants with moderate to severe MDD, aged 18-60, on SSRIs at least 6 weeks; healthy controls for MRI substudy
study.inclusion_criteria: participants with moderate to severe MDD moderate (score of 17-23) to severe MDD (score>=24) based on the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale-17 (HAMD-17) score, between the ages of 18 and 60 years, and administration of SSRIs at least 6 week. Healthy controls (HCs) with HAMD17<7 and no history of any psychotic disorders were included. All participants who received MRI scans were right-handed and free of contraindications to MRI.
study.exclusion_criteria: non-monophasic depression, drug or alcohol addiction, severe internal conditions and tumors, positive suicidal tendency, and previously treated with IA or participating in other clinical trials

arms.dropouts: 5 dropped out (2 considered ineffective, 1 failed to follow prescription, 1 private reasons, 1 failed to follow prescription)
4 dropped out (1 considered ineffective, 1 failed to follow prescription, 1 private reasons, 1 considered ineffective)
5 dropped out (1 considered ineffective, 2 private reasons, 1 intolerable IA-induced pain, 1 lost contact)
3 did not complete both scans; 2 excluded due to large head motions

extraction_notes.note: eTable 1 (detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria), eTable 2 (acupoint locations), eTable 3 (ROI definitions), eTable 4 (MDD comorbidities), eTable 5 (acupuncture expectation details), eTable 6 (MRI substudy baseline characteristics), eTable 7 (HAMD-17 five factor score details), eTable 8 (sedative-hypnotics), eTable 9 (compliance and blinding details), eTable 10 (full FC results MDD vs HC), eTable 11 (full FC results pre vs post IA), and eFig. 1 (experimental paradigm), eFig. 2 (MRI study flow) are all referenced but not available in the provided PDF. Detailed quantitative neuroimaging results (coordinates, cluster sizes, t-statistics) are in eTables 10 and 11 and could not be extracted.

Neuroimaging results (FC contrasts) are reported only narratively in the main text. Coordinates, cluster sizes, t-statistics, and exact p-values for all FC results are not provided in the main text; they are only cited as being in eTables 10 and 11 (supplements not provided). Consequently, all neural result entries are marked as 'narrative_only' with no coordinate data.

The exact n_analyzed for the MRI substudy contrasts is ambiguous. The paper states 20 MDD patients enrolled, 17 completed both scans, 2 excluded for head motion, implying n=15 for within-subject contrasts. For between-group MDD vs HC comparisons, n=15 MDD + 20 HC = 35 total. The paper states '20 HCs completed one MRI scan.' These values are used as best approximations but should be verified against eTables.

Table 2 reports primary outcome as 'mean (SD)' in the text (-9.6 [SD, 4.9]) but Table 2 column values appear to use SE format (e.g., -9.6 [0.8]). These may represent different reporting formats within the same table. Both are preserved: the abstract/text SD values and the table SE-format values.

The n_analyzed values in Table 2 reflect mITT completers at specific timepoints (SSRIs: n=36, SSRIs+SIA: n=37, SSRIs+AIA: n=36 at week 6; note these differ from the ITT n=40 per group). Missing data were handled by LOCF for ITT, but Table 2 appears to use mITT completers.

The Nausea row in Table 3 reports SSRIs as '8 (15.0%)' which is inconsistent with n=40 in that arm (15% of 40 = 6, not 8). This appears to be a typographical error in the paper; the value is preserved as reported: '8 (15.0)'.
Deqi or other needle sensation measures were not reported for any treatment group in the main text or any referenced supplementary materials. This is not discussed by the authors.

HAMD-17 five factor score data (detailed values for all five factors across all groups and timepoints) are only reported to be in eTable 7, which was not available. Only narrative statements about significance are extractable from the main text.

Figure 2 shows brain images labeled with region names (Frontal_Inf_Tri_L, Cerebelum_6_R for MDD>HC; Frontal_Inf_Tri_R, Cerebelum_9_L for post-IA<pre-IA) and seed names (VRP_R, DC_L, VRP_R, VSi_L), with color scale from -6 to +6 and coordinates Y=21, X=30, Y=27, X=-9. These appear to be MNI coordinates from figure captions but represent slices, not peak coordinates. They are not extracted as peak coordinates to avoid misinterpretation.

The paper describes the fMRI substudy MDD patients as a separate cohort of 20 (not sampled from the 120 RCT participants), but this is not made fully explicit. The arm 'arm_MDD_MRI' may partially overlap with the RCT arms. The paper notes 'randomization and blinding were not applicable' for the MRI study.

The abstract states 'IA enhanced FCs between striatum and frontal_inf_tri, and striatum and cerebellum.' However, the results section states that IA 'decreased FC between Striatum and left Cerebelum_9, right Frontal_Inf_Tri.' This represents a decrease in post-IA vs pre-IA. The abstract phrasing 'enhanced' appears to describe normalization (toward HC levels) rather than absolute increase. The raw direction (decreased post-IA vs pre-IA) is preserved as reported in the results section.
SSRIs dosage was acknowledged by the authors as a limitation: 'we did not analyze SSRIs dosage as a variable.' No dosage-stratified analyses are reported.
